recipes.name: Chicken Enchiladas Suizas
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) can diced green chile peppers
2 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, chopped
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a rapid boil over medium-high heat; add chicken breasts, cover, and cook until tender, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain and transfer chicken to a cutting board; use two forks to shred chicken and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 10x15-inch baking dish.

Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper in the melted butter until just soft, 5 to 8 minutes; transfer to a large bowl. Add shredded chicken, Cheddar cheese, green chile peppers, salsa, cilantro, cumin, and chipotle peppers to the bowl. Season with salt and pepper; mix.

Place about 1/3 cup of chicken mixture along the edge of a tortilla; roll tightly into a tube. Place enchilada, seam-side down, into the prepared baking dish. Repeat until all of the chicken mixture is used. Sprinkle Monterey Jack cheese over enchiladas. Whisk whipping cream and chicken broth together in a small bowl; pour over enchiladas. Cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Bake in preheated oven 30 minutes. Remove foil and continue baking until cheese is completely melted, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Enchiladas Suizas
raw_recipe.description: Enchiladas suizas, stuffed with shredded chicken, chiles, and green salsa, are topped with a cheesy creamy white sauce and baked until bubbling and delicious.

review.reviewBody: Got lazy and instead of making individual enchiladas, lined a large baking dish with corn tortillas (gluten-free), put the chicken mixture in, covered with more tortillas and covered witht the cheese and cream and baked it, it worked well.

My friends and family have loved this recipe. I made it the first time with the recommended double serving of cream sauce. I definitely think that is necessary. The second time, I replaced a cup of heavy whipping cream with 8 oz of cream cheese. THAT was pretty amazing. It thickens things up a little and makes the whole dish just a little creamier. Try it!

This was super yummy. I had a few tweaks: roasted chicken breast on the bone in the oven (super juicy) or use store bought roast chicken. Instead of adding the green chili's to the chicken, I pureed them in a food processor with the chicken stock and then added the cream. The kicker is to add extra cheese to the top of the enchiladas before covering with the creamy sauce mixture and letting casserole sit for 20 mins before cutting into. The sauce was a perfect consistency!. I wish I had taken a photo :( Next time!

Fabulous recipe. I made a few adjustments though. I boiled the chicken in chicken broth for 10 minutes then set it on low for an hour before shredding it. Chicken came out amazingly moist. I used corn tortillas. I briefly fried the tortillas in a small bit of olive oil to soften them before rolling the enchiladas. I used a combination of queso fresco and Montery Jack cheese for the topping. I added about 1/2 cup of sour cream to sauce after reading other reviews about the sauce being too watery. Husband said these were the best chicken enchiladas he's had... even better than any restaurant.

Wow wow wow. I didn't have any adobo peppers so I substituted for 2 finely chopped jalapeños and cooked them for the last 2-3 min with the onions and bell peppers. The meat mixture made too much for 12 tortillas so we had enough leftover to repurpose for a yummy Mexican brunch dish! After 10 min baking without the foil I broiled for 1 additional minute to get a bit of charred bubbliness on the cheese. My husband was so stuffed but refused to stop eating until his plate was clean!!! This was a crowd pleaser we will definitely be adding to our rotation of dinner recipes.

Made this for a birthday party last night-everyone enjoyed. I did make two changes: 1. used a rotisserie chicken from Costco for chicken meat - great time saver 2. did not put green chilies in the filling, instead I used them in the sauce which I substituted from another recipe on this site. The sauce is 1/4 c. butter, 1/4 c. flour- melt butter, stir in flour and cook several minutes. Stir in 2 c. chicken broth and heat until thickened. Off heat, whisk in 1 c. sour cream and 4 oz green chilies. Pour over enchiladas and then top with cheese. Bake per recipe instructions. The heat of this dish is on the milder side, so I think I will add green chilies to the filling next time. Definitely will make again.

I suggest much higher oven temp (400) and no foil, since all ingredients are warm and high heat is needed to evaporate and condense the creamy broth; this also shortens cooking time. Also, heads up, chipotle peppers are hot without the seeds, so definitely do REMOVE THE SEEDS inside the peppers, chop finely, and distribute evenly throughout mixture. I eliminated the canned green chile peppers, cilantro and green salsa. Therefore, for my scaled down 4 tortillas, I moistened the mix with just a 1/4 cup of regular salsa. In place of chicken broth, try tasty liquid from canned Goya Chickpeas in Sauce.
I also double the cream and chicken broth... family favorite!

I made this for 13 people, doubled the recipe. Everything was perfect. For the sauce I did 1 cup of sour cream, 1 cup of whipping cream, and 1-1/2 cup of broth. I boiled it over low heat to thicken. I didn't want it too thick but not too thin. It soaked up perfectly.

Am I the only one who had trouble figuring out what to do with the chicken after it was cooked? Shredded it, and then ended up chopping it a little finer in the food processor. If using 1 chicken breast/person, breast should be small. I had major leftover filling (not necessarily a bad thing). Also, I always forget to spray the aluminum foil so the cheese doesn't stick. Wrote it on my recipe to remember next time. Like others, I doubled the sauce and substituted 8 oz. cream cheese for 1C whipping cream. Served w/sour cream on the side at the table.

Tremendous flavors and great leftover.

The recipe has no directions of what to do with the chicken after it is boiled just to add it to the peppers etc.. Is it supposed to be chopped? Shredded? I doubt it’s supposed to be left whole. Also change the whipping cream and chicken broth proportions in the recipe not just as a note . I got home from the store then barely noticed it under the title .
The flour tortillas were very mushy, reminded me of white bread.
Delicious and a big hit. I added 1/4 cup salsa to sauce to give some flavor. It thickened up perfectly.

This is a tasty recipe, just not one for us. The filling was full of flavor, but just too many flavors. The chipotles, the salsa verde, and the chile flavors don't mingle well in my opinion, and it just wasn't for us. I was skeptical about the sauce, but it was delicious. I think with some personalization, I would make this recipe again. I halved the recipe and I garnished with chopped cilantro and finely diced red peppers. It would also be nice to have a weight measurement for the chicken, as chicken breasts come in all sizes. I used ONE large chicken breast to make 6 enchiladas.
I think this recipe is amazing! This is the second time I have made it. love it!

Loved it! This will become a go-to for me. These are far better than any enchiladas you can buy or even get in a restaurant. They definately take longer than the stated 20 minutes of prep time, but they're worth it. I didn't add the hot peppers because my mom and husband won't eat them, but I was otherwise true to the recipe. They even looked like gourmet enchiladas!

Loved it! Took a lot longer to prep than 20 minutes, but it was worth the effort. Flavorful and came out looking like restaurant quality food. I took out the hot peppers because both my mom and husband can't take any spice.
awsome recipe thank you
